title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from p.11): Y is a space. An abstract conical ('tubular') neighbourhood of Y is a space T containing Y, with a closed subset Ṫ (the 'boundary of the tube') and an action I×T→T of the multiplicative topological monoid I=[0,1]. The action fixes Y pointwise, sends 0·T into Y, and makes T the pushout (I×Ṫ) ∪_{0×Ṫ} Y. In other words T is the mapping cylinder C(f) of f: Ṫ→Y, f(x)=0·x, with its radial I-action. T̊ = T∖Ṫ = ∪_{λ<1} λT.

This page:
(i) The sets T_λ=λT (λ∈[0,1]) form an increasing family of closed subsets of T. In the cylinder picture T_λ is the image of [0,λ]×Ṫ ⊔ Y. The sets T̊_λ := λT̊ (λ∈]0,1]) form an increasing family of open subsets, the image of [0,λ[×Ṫ ⊔ Y.
(ii) For 0<λ<1, T̊_λ is exactly the topological interior of T_λ in T. For λ=1 this fails: T̊_1=T̊ is not the interior of T_1=T in T (which is T itself), unless Ṫ=∅, i.e. T=Y.
(iii) Definition (6). For ε=1-λ∈]0,1[, Ep_ε(T) := T∖T̊_{1-ε} is the 'thickening of index ε' of the boundary Ṫ in T, i.e. the band between (1-ε)Ṫ and Ṫ. Its frontier in T is (1-ε)Ṫ, and it is a neighbourhood of Ṫ in T.
(iv) (7) Via (λ,x)↦λx, Ep_ε(T) ≅ [1-ε,1]×Ṫ. So Ṫ has a collar in T; this prepares the notion of 'partie bonne' (collared closed subspace) on the next page.
(v) Margin remark: if the T_ε form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of Y in T (true e.g. under a compactness hypothesis; not automatic for the quotient topology of a mapping cylinder with non-compact Ṫ), then they also form one in the ambient space X.
(vi) ② Relative version. Let Y⊂X be closed. A conical neighbourhood of Y in X is a neighbourhood T of Y in X carrying such an I-action. Then the λT (λ∈]0,1]) are again tubular neighbourhoods of Y in X, forming an increasing family. Claim (8): for 0<λ<1, Ṫ_λ = λṪ is the frontier of T_λ in X. The next page notes that this fails for λ=1: Ṫ need not be the frontier of T in X.

Purpose: a purely topological, monoid-action axiomatics of mapping-cylinder (conical) neighbourhoods of strata. It is the basic building block for 'déploiement' of stratified spaces, i.e. replacing a stratified space by a manifold-with-corners-like 'unfolded' object via collars and tubes. This is in the spirit of the tame-topology programme of Esquisse §5.
errors: Claim (8) needs an extra hypothesis. As stated (T only a neighbourhood of Y in X), points of T̊ away from Y may lie on the frontier of T in X, so λT̊ need not be open in X. Counterexample: X = T-shaped graph [0,1]×{0} ∪ {1/2}×[0,1], Y={(0,0)}, T=[0,1]×{0} with radial action; for λ=3/4 the frontier of T_λ in X contains (1/2,0) besides λṪ=(3/4,0). One needs T̊ open in X (equivalently, the frontier of T in X is contained in Ṫ).

The displayed formula Ep_ε(T)=Ṫ ∪ (1-ε)·Ṫ, read literally, is only two copies of Ṫ. What is meant (per (6) and (7)) is the band ∪_{1-ε≤μ≤1} μṪ ≅ [1-ε,1]×Ṫ; the bold 'U' is presumably shorthand for this.

The margin remark rightly flags that the T_ε need not be a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of Y in the quotient (mapping-cylinder) topology when Ṫ is non-compact. The main text does not otherwise address this; it is a gap rather than an error.

ideas.what: Abstract conical/tubular neighbourhood as a space with an action of the multiplicative monoid [0,1], identified with the mapping cylinder of the 'end' map Ṫ→Y; nested family λT and the interiors λT̊
ideas.modern_name: mapping cylinder neighbourhood / teardrop neighbourhood; control data (tubular functions) in Thom–Mather theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970) for control data; Siebenmann (1972) and Quinn (1988) for mapping cylinder/homotopy-link neighbourhoods; Hughes for teardrops
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tubular neighbourhoods and the 'déploiement' of stratified spaces informally; no detailed axiomatics published

ideas.what: Collar of the boundary: Ep_ε(T) ≅ [1-ε,1]×Ṫ, with frontier (1-ε)Ṫ
ideas.modern_name: collar of a boundary; collared subspace

ideas.what: Relative conical neighbourhood of a closed subspace Y⊂X and the frontier statement (8)
ideas.modern_name: regular / mapping-cylinder neighbourhood of a stratum

deep.surprise_reason: Routine point-set groundwork: basic properties of mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods and collars, phrased elegantly via an action of the monoid ([0,1],·). Nothing beyond standard material; it contains a small gap (openness of T̊ in X).
transcription_corrections: 'est tel et bien l'intérieur' should read 'est bel et bien l'intérieur'.
'Le frontière de E_ε' should read 'La frontière de E_ε'.
The leading '(5)' is a renumbered marker, probably '(5 bis)' or a struck '(5)', before 'NB les T_λ'.
The end of the NB line after 'E_ε est un voisinage de Ṫ' seems to carry an isolated word 'bon', anticipating 'partie bonne' on the next page.
In (7), '(sous λ)' is the label λ placed under the interval, i.e. the coordinate is λ: Ep_ε(T) ≅ [1-ε,1]×Ṫ.

The margin NB likely reads: 'NB si les T_ε (ε∈]0,1]) forment un système fondamental de voisinages de Y dans T (… compact?), alors les T_ε forment un système fondamental de voisinages de Y dans X'. It is not 'Y∖T_ε'.

In ②, 'Un voisinage conique' carries the inserted word 'conique' (underlined) together with 'de Y dans X'. The struck passage reads roughly 'faisant de T un vois. top. conique absolu de Y satisfaisant les conditions dites'.
Formula (8) is written below the last line as 'Ṫ_λ = λṪ est la frontière de T_λ = λT dans X'.
